flashcards.q: SQS Standard vs FIFO throughput limits?
flashcards.a: Standard: nearly unlimited API calls/sec. FIFO: 300 TPS unbatched, 3,000/sec batched, up to 30,000 TPS with high-throughput mode enabled (relaxed ordering across, not within, message groups).

flashcards.q: What causes the classic SQS duplicate-processing bug?
flashcards.a: Visibility timeout set shorter than the handler's actual processing time -- the message becomes visible to a second consumer while the first is still working it, so both process it. Fix: raise the timeout above p99 runtime (or extend dynamically) AND add an idempotency key as defense-in-depth.
Exactly-once processing within a 5-minute deduplication window, via content-based dedup (SHA-256 hash of the body) or an explicit MessageDeduplicationId.

flashcards.q: SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge -- one-word model for each?
flashcards.a: SQS = mailbox (one consumer per message, buffered). SNS = megaphone (fan-out to every subscriber). EventBridge = switchboard (content-based routing via rules across multiple sources/targets).

flashcards.q: What can EventBridge do natively that SNS+SQS cannot?
flashcards.a: Content-based routing on full JSON event structure (not just attributes), a schema registry that tracks/versions event shapes, and native archive + replay of events matching a pattern.

flashcards.q: Step Functions Standard vs Express: pricing model and max duration?
flashcards.a: Standard: $0.025/1,000 state transitions, up to 1 year runtime, exactly-once. Express: ~$1/million requests plus duration/memory, max 5 minutes, at-least-once (async) or at-most-once (sync).

flashcards.q: Cost delta between Standard and Express Step Functions at volume?
flashcards.a: A 5-state workflow run 10 million times: roughly $1,250/month on Standard vs roughly $31/month on Express -- a 40x+ difference driven by per-state-transition billing.

flashcards.q: API Gateway REST vs HTTP API pricing and default recommendation?
flashcards.a: REST: $3.50/million requests, full feature set (usage plans, validation, native WAF). HTTP API: $1.00/million (~70% cheaper), covers ~90% of use cases -- the default choice unless a REST-only feature is specifically needed.

flashcards.q: When does ALB+Fargate beat API Gateway on cost?
flashcards.a: At sustained high request volume -- API Gateway's per-request pricing scales linearly forever, while ALB+Fargate's cost is roughly fixed within a provisioned capacity. Cited estimate: a modest ALB+Fargate setup runs ~$40-90/month in fixed cost regardless of volume within that capacity.

flashcards.q: Why is idempotency non-optional across this entire service list?
flashcards.a: At-least-once delivery is the DEFAULT guarantee across SQS, SNS, EventBridge target invocation, and Step Functions Express -- not an edge case. The fix is a dedup key checked via an ATOMIC conditional write (never read-then-write) before any side effect.

flashcards.q: What does a Step Functions state's Retry and Catch field do?
flashcards.a: Retry (ErrorEquals, IntervalSeconds, MaxAttempts, BackoffRate) handles transient failures declaratively. Catch matches specific error types to a fallback state for graceful handling -- Step Functions' built-in equivalent of resilience-catalogue retry/circuit-breaker patterns, expressed in the state machine definition rather than app code.

flashcards.q: An SQS FIFO message dedup by content hash is wrong for what kind of event?
flashcards.a: Events that can legitimately repeat with identical content but different real-world meaning (e.g. repeated identical button-click events) -- content-based dedup can't distinguish them. Use an explicit, producer-generated unique MessageDeduplicationId instead.
